## Overview

### The Problem

Book lovers face information overload:

- Hard to know which books are truly worth reading
- No way to see aggregate sentiment across thousands of reviews
- Difficult to find books on specific topics (e.g., forex trading, stoic philosophy)
- Reviews scattered across Reddit, Goodreads, Amazon, and forums

### The Solution

This platform aggregates and analyzes book reviews:

| Component | Technology | Status |
|:---|:---|:---|
| **Multi-Source Scraping** | Open Library, Google Books, Reddit | ✅ Live |
| **Sentiment Analysis** | VADER + TextBlob + Custom Rules | ✅ Live |
| **SQLite Database** | Lightweight & Portable | ✅ Live |
| **Interactive Dashboard** | Streamlit + Plotly | ✅ **Deployed** |
| **Word Clouds** | Visual keyword analysis | ✅ Live |
| **Search & Filter** | By category, sentiment, keyword | ✅ Live |

## Dashboard Features

### 📊 Sentiment Distribution
- Pie chart showing positive, neutral, negative reviews
- Overall sentiment score

### 📚 Book Library
- Browse all books with covers
- Filter by category
- Search by title, author, topic

### 💬 Review Analysis
- Top positive and negative reviews
- Sentiment scores per review
- Source attribution

### ☁️ Word Cloud
- Visual representation of common themes
- Top keywords by frequency
- Category-specific word analysis

### 🔍 Advanced Search
- Search for any topic (e.g., "forex trading")
- Find relevant books and discussions
- See sentiment for your interests

## Running Locally

```bash
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/gondamol/book-sentiment-analysis.git
cd book-sentiment-analysis

# Create virtual environment
python3 -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate

# Install dependencies
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Run the scraper
python scripts/scrape_books.py

# Run sentiment analysis
python scripts/analyze_sentiment.py

# Start the dashboard
streamlit run dashboard/app.py
```
